newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister vows to create 2,000 rural jobs.
newsitem.headline: French minister vows to create 2,000 rural jobs.

text.p: French Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur promised on Wednesday the government would create 2,000 jobs in the agricultural sector.

"We are in the process of identifying 2,000 jobs, which will be offered to young people at the Agricultural Show," he told a news conference on a French draft bill on agriculture. The annual show, held in Paris, runs from February 23 to March 2.
"We have the potential to create jobs which have not begun to be explored," he said, emphasising the possibilities in farming, agri-business and forestry.
The issue was critical for rural areas and the future of agriculture, he added. He did not say what the jobs would entail or who would pay for them.
The pledge to create rural jobs was the second government initiative in less than a week aimed at curbing France's acute 25 percent youth unemployment.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe announced after a marathon meeting with industry, union and student leaders on Monday an agreement to ease the passage from school to work.

The issue of unemployment, now at a record 12.7 percent nationally, will be crucial in next year's parliamentary elections. Rural votes carry significant political weight in France, Europe's largest food producing nation and where 85 percent of the country's land is covered by farms or forests.

Vasseur said the new farm law, outlines of which were discussed in cabinet on Wednesday, would prepare farmers for new market pressures in the years ahead while encouraging them to put the quality of food first.

French farmers took to the streets and burned tyres in opposition to cuts in European Union farm subsidies in 1992 and many fear further cuts in support as the EU prepares to expand eastwards at the start of the next century.
Vasseur said his bill would encourage farmers to become competitive on world markets but would put a big focus on jobs.
France's largest farm union, the FNSEA, said Vasseur's proposals had failed to lift uncertainty over farmers' incomes.
